newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees T-bill yield drop to Eurobond level.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees T-bill yield drop to Eurobond level.

text.p: Russian Treasury bill yields will soon fall to the level of the yield on the Russian Eurobond, Central Bank First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Wednesday.
He told Reuters Financial Television that January/February foreign buying of T-bills was stable and running at about $1 billion.
Aleksashenko also said that most foreigners would not be affected by a new 15 percent profits tax on government securities, which he said had caused confusion in the market.
Many non-residents' profits on the income are covered by double taxation treaties.
Aleksashenko said the Central Bank had more than $10 billion in reserves and was controlling the situation on Russian financial markets.
He said the Central Bank was currently only buying foreign currency on the interbank market. Russia had sold $1.5 billion in January after buying several hundred million dollars in December.
"The Central Bank is in full control of the financial markets and its intervention has fully neutralised the extra liquidity which had existed," he said.

Non-resident funds into government securities and proceeds from Russia's debut Eurobond had affected market liquidity and forced active Central Bank intervention in January, he said, adding that initial efforts had not "pushed the market down".
"The situation has changed significantly in the first 10 days of February," he said. "The Central Bank is only buying hard currency."

He said that non-residents, who he said were investing about $1 billion a month in government securities in January and February, would generally not be affected by a new 15 percent profits tax on new treasury bills.
"Russia has dozens of double-taxation treaties," he said.
He said that the bank had forecast falling rates in January and that rates on government securities would fall further.

"We control the reserves and have the ability to bring about a long-term decrease in yields on Russian paper, and we predict that yields on T-bills will soon become closer to that of the dollar-denominated Eurobond."
The 0.25 percent November 2001 Eurobond currently yields about 9.55 percent, while T-bills maturing in June-August this year are yielding 27-28 percent.
